exposure: cast type (short-leg vs. long-leg spica casts)
outcome: treatment failure (re-dislocation, imaging-confirmed reduction loss, or surgical conversion)
cohort: The study included 146 developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH) patients, aged 0-18 months, who underwent closed reduction and spica cast treatment at two tertiary centers.
finding: Long-leg spica casts demonstrated significantly higher 6-month incident-free survival rates and were identified as an independent protective factor against treatment failure compared to short-leg spica casts.
mod_finding: Delivery mode did not reach statistical significance as a predictor of treatment failure.
